entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sun He (died 204 CE), a formidable military general and an adopted son of the warlord Sun Jian, was a pivotal figure in the foundational years of the Eastern Wu regime during the tumultuous late Eastern Han dynasty. Operating primarily in the lower Yangtze River region, Sun He's strategic prowess and loyalty were instrumental in securing and expanding the territorial base for his foster brothers Sun Ce and later Sun Quan, ultimately contributing to the establishment of one of the Three Kingdoms. His career encapsulates the volatile period of fragmentation and consolidation that preceded the formal division of China, highlighting the critical role of trusted commanders in forging new dynastic power.

Sun He's military career began under his adoptive father Sun Jian, participating in campaigns against the Yellow Turban rebels and the coalition against Dong Zhuo. Following Sun Jian's death, he served Sun Ce, distinguishing himself in numerous engagements that saw the rapid conquest of territories like Kuaiji and Wu commanderies. He was appointed Administrator of Kuaiji, a key coastal region, and later commanded forces in the critical defense of Wu's northern borders against challenges from Cao Cao's forces. His leadership was crucial during the Battle of Liyang in 204 CE, where he successfully repelled an invasion, though he tragically died in the same year, possibly from wounds sustained or an internal purge related to a separate incident involving bandits.
